title: John Lewis discount code cuts LEGO prices even further
summary: A new John Lewis code, LEGOAUGUST, stacks extra savings on top of already-reduced LEGO sets, pushing some prices to new lows.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
John Lewis has launched a new discount code, LEGOAUGUST, which applies to LEGO sets already marked down in its sale. The tiered code gives shoppers £10 off spends of £70+, £15 off £100+, and £45 off £300+.

Because John Lewis also price-matches other retailers, stacking this code on top of existing discounts has produced some notably low prices, including 11381 Jaguar E-Type at £101.99, 76466 Philosopher's Stone Collectors' Edition at £93.99, and 75192 Millennium Falcon at £594.99. Smaller sets can also be combined to hit the £100 threshold - for example, pairing 76463 Hogwarts Castle: Hospital Wing (£66.99) with 76470 Enchanted Flying Ford Anglia (£42.99) brings the total to £109.98 after the code, a £50 saving overall.

Eligible sets are marked with a red 'view offers' logo on the John Lewis site.

## Why it matters
For UK LEGO fans and collectors, this is a straightforward way to save extra cash on sets that are already discounted, especially useful if you're building a collection, hunting a specific display piece, or topping up a stadium or large-scale build. Bundling smaller sets to clear spending thresholds is a handy tactic worth knowing.

## What to watch next
Discount codes like this are typically time-limited, so it's worth checking current eligibility and stock on the John Lewis site before assuming a price will hold.

title: LEGO Ministry of Magic review flags seven design gripes
summary: Brick Fanatics' hands-on review of 76476 Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition highlights seven design shortcomings, from missing minifigures to an unusually high sticker count, along with suggested fixes.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has published a hands-on review of the upcoming 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition, calling out seven specific design issues they found puzzling. Highlights include an empty courtroom scene missing key minifigures (Cornelius Fudge and Amelia Bones, neither of whom appear in the main set), and a heavy reliance on stickers – 32 in total – for details like hand dryers and a telephone box phone that the reviewer feels could have been brick-built instead.

Notably, Fudge does appear, but only in the separate limited-time gift-with-purchase set 40901 Ministry Munchies & The Daily Prophet Stands, not in the main Ministry of Magic set itself.

## Why it matters
For Harry Potter LEGO fans and collectors, minifigure line-up and build quality often make or break a big-ticket set like this. If genuine gaps exist in character selection or finishing touches, it's useful for prospective buyers to know before committing to what's likely a premium-priced Collectors' Edition.

title: LEGO Harry Potter 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition: review verdict is in
summary: Brick Fanatics has published its review of the new LEGO Harry Potter Collectors' Edition set, and it's a rare miss for the subtheme, scoring just 4/10 overall.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has reviewed 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition, the latest large-scale LEGO Harry Potter set, giving it an overall score of 4/10. The set follows on from the well-received Burrow and Hogsmeade Collectors' Edition sets, but the reviewer says this one struggles across the board.

According to the review, the design splits the Ministry of Magic across multiple underground levels beneath a London street scene, echoing the layered approach used in the Gringotts Wizarding Bank Collectors' Edition set. It covers familiar Order of the Phoenix locations including the Hall of Prophecy, the Death Chamber, the Wizengamot courtroom, and the offices of Umbridge and Arthur Weasley.

The breakdown scores given were Design 3/10, Playability 2/10, Value 5/10, Minifigures 6/10, and Build 6/10. Positives highlighted include the London street level and some new printed pieces, while criticisms focus on an overly ambitious concept, visible cost-cutting on minifigures, and pricing that the reviewer feels doesn't match what's on offer.

This follows the theme's only previous take on the location, 76403 The Ministry of Magic, a smaller 990-piece playset focused on the atrium and fountain.

## Why it matters
Collectors' Edition sets are LEGO Harry Potter's flagship, premium-price releases, so a weak review from a trusted outlet like Brick Fanatics is a useful heads-up for anyone considering the set, especially given the higher cost typically attached to this subtheme.

The clip shows a retro computer booting up with racing-themed readouts like 'Driver Telemetry Database' and 'Mechanic Status', plus a 1988 calendar, a yellow brick, and yellow-and-black headphones in shot.

Fans have pointed out that 1988 was the year Ayrton Senna won his first Formula One World Drivers' Championship, driving the McLaren MP4/4 — a car LEGO already turned into a 693-piece Icons set in 2024, complete with a Senna minifigure and mini helmet. The colours shown in the teaser also echo Senna's iconic yellow, green and blue helmet design, which itself drew inspiration from the Brazilian flag.

This would follow on from LEGO's Editions theme, which has already released four Formula 1 helmet sets in 2026. Importantly, LEGO has not officially confirmed a Senna helmet set — this is currently speculation based on the teaser's clues.

## Why it matters
If accurate, this would be the second Senna-related LEGO product, following the MP4/4 Icons set, and would extend the Editions helmet line-up that's already proven popular with F1 and motorsport fans this year. For collectors building out a racing-themed display, another high-profile driver helmet would be a welcome addition — but it's worth waiting for LEGO to confirm details before getting too excited.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants: comparing the 2006 and 2026 Bikini Bottom sets
summary: Brick Fanatics has compared the original 2006 Bikini Bottom set with the newly reviewed 2026 version, showing just how far LEGO design has come in two decades.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has put the original 2006 LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants set, 3827 Adventures in Bikini Bottom, side by side with the newly released 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom set, which marks the theme's 20th anniversary.

According to the outlet, the 2006 set contained 579 pieces and three minifigures, while the 2026 set has grown to 1,794 pieces, still with three minifigures included. Both sets depict the three houses on Conch Street along with some extra side builds, but the piece count has nearly quadrupled.

The biggest changes highlighted are in minifigure design. The SpongeBob minifigure has moved away from a standard body with a printed torso element, to an entirely new, larger body sculpt built with Technic pin connections. This allows separate arm pieces (similar to those used for Minions) to be attached, better representing SpongeBob's sleeves. His legs are also newly dual-moulded to show his socks and shoes, and his overall colour has been updated to a paler, more accurate shade compared with the original figure.

## Why it matters
For collectors and long-time LEGO fans, this comparison is a handy snapshot of how much minifigure design, piece counts and detailing have evolved over 20 years. It also gives a clearer picture of what's included in the new 11386 set beyond a simple piece count, which is useful if you're deciding whether to add it to a display or collection.

## What to watch next
Brick Fanatics' full review of 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom is worth checking for more detail on pricing, build experience and how it fits alongside other LEGO licensed theme sets.

title: LEGO Harry Potter's New GWP Doesn't Quite Fit Its Companion Set
summary: LEGO has revealed 40901 Ministry Munchies & The Daily Prophet Stands as a free gift with Harry Potter purchases, timed to launch alongside 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition — but fans have spotted a design mismatch between the two.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially revealed 40901 Ministry Munchies & The Daily Prophet Stands, a gift-with-purchase (GWP) set arriving alongside 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition, which launches 29 August.

The GWP will be free with LEGO Harry Potter orders over £115 / $130 / €130 for a limited time, and includes small market stalls plus a second Fountain of Magical Brethren, featuring a golden witch minifigure built using a new recoloured hairpiece.

Here's the snag: in the books, the fountain is a single structure, but the films split it into two separate fountains — one with a wizard, tricorn hat and skull (already included in the main 76476 set), and another featuring a witch, centaur, goblin and house-elf. The GWP only recreates the witch element of that second fountain, not the full grouping.

Even at this reduced scale, there isn't obvious room for it inside 76476's Ministry atrium without sacrificing the space set aside for the Dumbledore vs Voldemort duel scene. You could try swapping out the original fountain, but the GWP's base tier is reportedly still too large to fit comfortably.

## Why it matters
GWPs are usually designed as neat little extras that complement a flagship set, so builders eyeing 76476 might reasonably expect this fountain piece to slot straight in. Instead, anyone hoping to display the two together may need to get creative with space — or accept that a chunk of the freebie won't have a natural home in the main build.

## What to watch next
It's worth checking official LEGO Harry Potter product pages nearer the 29 August release for final GWP thresholds and availability, as promotional gift-with-purchase terms can vary by region and change close to launch.
